page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data places this instance in the average tier across most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor supports AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI instructions, contributing to a PassMark CPU score of 9028.43 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4867.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 50.86 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 38.65 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance exhibits performance limitations in specific workloads, such as Redis SET operations, which scored in the bottom 25% at 7.55 million operations per second, and medium-sized LLM inference (7B model), which registered poor prompt processing speeds of 11.62 tokens per second.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.hfr6.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or intensive GPU acceleration. It is suitable for relational database hosting, in-memory caching with moderate write requirements, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less suited for large-scale language model inference or high-throughput write-heavy database workloads.
